design_analysis:
1. CSS CUSTOM PROPERTIES (verbatim from the :root block, lines 8-9) --bg:#0a0e14; near-black, blue-shifted navy --panel:#111823; card/note surface, one step up from bg --line:#1e2a38; 1px hairlines: card borders, table row rules (rows use rgba(30,42,56,.5), i.e. the same hue at half alpha) --fg:#e6edf3; near-white body and heading text --dim:#8b9bb0; secondary text, table headers, .sub, .lose cells --ok:#3fb950; green — pass/win cells, t-ok tags --warn:#d29922; amber — note.warn border, t-warn tags --bad:#f85149; red — the FLUX.2 ZH 0.757 cell, t-bad tags --acc:#58a6ff; blue — links, hover border, .note left border Two off-palette support colours exist and should be treated as fixed: #c9d5e3 (body copy inside .card/.note/li) and #0d1420 (code and 
 background, slightly darker than --panel).
   Status tags are tint-on-tint, not solid fills: rgba(colour,.4) border + rgba(colour,.08) fill. The whole design is a low-saturation, high-contrast readout.

2. INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE (single centred column, .wrap max-width 1000px, top to bottom)
   a. Header — h1 'VidiFlow - Image Model Reports' + .sub line stating scope and date. Two lines, then a 24px gap. No navigation.
   b. Section 'The reports - click to open' — three full-width  links. Each card is a name, a t-ok size tag, and one sentence of description ending in a bolded verdict. These are the primary actions of the page; they are the first thing below the header and are visually the heaviest objects in the top third.
   c. Section 'Local - top 5' — a 5-column table (#, Model, Text evidence, Disk, License), ranked 1-5. Green class="win" marks the best scores and MIT licenses; grey class="lose" marks non-commercial licenses; one red inline span marks the bad CJK score. Right-aligned tabular-nums for disk sizes.
   d. .note (blue accent bar) — the report's thesis: the baseline is ~3 characters in 4 correct and no setting fixes it; the official recipe measured worse at 3x the cost.
   e. .card 'HiDream-O1 needs one file, not three' — the architecture/VRAM argument, plus a bolded caveat that the #1 pick's text scores are author-reported and VRAM peak is unmeasured.
   f. Section 'Paid - keep three' — a 4-column table (#, Model, Cost @1K, Why), one row explicitly demoted with a greyed verdict and an inline quality retirement date.
   g. .note.warn (amber bar) — explains why benchmarks pass while the user's real pages fail: benchmarks used short quoted strings with an explicit 'render exactly' instruction.
   h. .card 'Two things worth knowing before you build on this' — the CJK-grader warning (a vision-LLM grader silently corrected 14 Chinese strings) and the FLUX.2 ranking contradiction between two benchmarks.
   i. Section 'Recommended next step' — a .card with the plan (pull two models, ~12.3 GB, both MIT, run a character-exact transcription test) and a 
 block of three URLs.
   j. Footer line — the provenance promise: every price tagged primary / third-party / unverified, no estimates presented as facts.
   There is no sidebar, no header bar, no footer nav, no imagery of any kind, and no element wider than the 1000px column.

3. VISUAL TONE, AND WHAT FITS VS WHAT CLASHES
   The tone is a bench instrument reading out a verdict: dark instrument panel, hairline rules, monospace only where actual code or numbers appear, semantic colour used sparingly and only as meaning (pass / caution / fail / link). Everything is quiet, flat, dense, and legible. The page's authority comes from looking like it was measured, not designed.
   FITS: near-black grounds so the image dissolves into --bg; low-saturation cool palette with one restrained warm accent; shallow depth of field so the subject is a single held focus; visible material texture (anodised metal, frosted acrylic, ceramic, matte composite); hard directional key light rather than soft studio wash; single subject, uncluttered frame; the same 1px-hairline discipline expressed as physical seams or edges; a sense of something measured or forensic rather than something decorative.
   CLASHES: anything with large areas of saturated colour (a green/red brand-field would collide with --ok/--bad and destroy their meaning); anything soft, dreamy, pastel, or bokeh-heavy, which would read as stock photography against a page that reads as instrumentation; high-key white or light backgrounds, which would flash a white block into a near-black page; busy all-over detail or dense particle fields, which would compete with two tables for the eye; lens flares, HDR glow, chromatic aberration, heavy vignetting; human faces or figures, which introduce a narrative this page has no use for; anything 3D-rendered-and-shiny with a product-advertising sheen.
   Critically: any image containing lettering, digits, a HUD, a gauge with numbers, or a chart axis would (a) fight the page's real typography for authority, and (b) be an outright liability in a report whose entire thesis is that generated text is only ~75% character-exact. The no-text constraint here is not a style preference; it is the thesis of the document.

4. WHERE THE READER'S EYE ACTUALLY GOES, AND WHERE AN ILLUSTRATION EARNS ITS PLACE
   The eye path is: h1 -> the three report cards (b, largest and highest-contrast objects) -> the first table (c, densest block) -> .note (d) -> the two cards -> the second table -> the next-step card -> footer. The tables and the two blue/amber notes carry the reading; the cards are scan targets.
   Three claims on this page are stated in prose but are SPATIAL or PROPORTIONAL facts that prose cannot make a reader feel. Those are the only defensible places for an image, because an image's real job is to make a quantity or a structure visible rather than to decorate a surface.
     - '22.4 GB on a 22.5 GB card - zero headroom' and 'one file, not three' (section e). This is a volume-vs-payload fact stated as two numbers. A reader can quote it but cannot picture zero headroom, and cannot see that three components plus an upcast duplicate overflow a container that one compact component clears easily. An image of one tray holding an overhanging stack beside a single unit with empty floor around it makes the argument in one glance.
     - 'Your baseline is ~3 characters in 4 correct, not 100%' (section d, the thesis). The number is the most important claim in the document and currently exists only as bold text. A field of identical tiles in which a minority are subtly defective lets the reader's own eye find the failures, which is the whole point: the defect rate is ORDINARY, not dramatic.
     - 'author-reported', 'No independent OCR benchmark exists yet', and the footer promise 'Every price tagged primary / third-party / unverified' (sections e, h, j). The report's epistemic spine - that its own numbers do not all carry the same weight - is currently encoded in one italic phrase, two hedges, and a 12.5px dim footer nobody reads. A stack of specimen plates at visibly different grades of finish, with one slot empty, encodes graded confidence without a single word.
   Everything else on the page is already either self-evident from the type or already better served by the markup.

5. COUNT JUSTIFICATION - WHY THREE, NOT FIVE
   Three is the number of spatial facts the page asserts and cannot show. One image per claim, no more, because each additional image in a 1000px single-column scroll costs roughly half a screen of a reader's attention and buys nothing the prose does not already carry. I specifically rejected a fourth and fifth rather than pad the set; see the 'rejected' array for the eight candidates I considered and cut. I also cut the two-square-over-one-wide alternatives: making all three wide would have made the page feel like a magazine rather than an instrument readout, and the two square images are content-shaped (a grid, a stack) and will sit at roughly 380-420px beside or under a note without dominating the column.

6. HONEST UNCERTAINTY
   Two of the three prompts are asking a diffusion model for something it is only moderately good at, and I want that on the record rather than buried.
   - Image 'imperfect-baseline-field' asks for a REGULAR GRID IN WHICH A SPECIFIC MINORITY OF TILES ARE SUBTLY DEFECTIVE. Diffusion models are notoriously weak at exact countable structure; the 'one in four' may not survive rendering, and the reader may be unable to count the failures. If the render does not hold, this image should be cut rather than retried indefinitely - the honest fallback is no image there and the thesis stays as bold text.
   - Image 'evidence-grade-plates' asks the viewer to read 'graded confidence' from differing surface finish, and to read one EMPTY slot as 'the independent benchmark that does not exist'. The finish-grading should work because it is a material cue. The empty slot is a weaker signal and may simply read as unused space; if so it is still harmless, but do not expect a reader to name it.
   - Image 'vram-headroom-tray' is the one I am most confident in, because a stack overhanging a rim and a single unit sitting in clear floor are both ordinary, high-frequency visual facts that models render reliably. Its one risk is the divider seam being elaborated into an arrow or a label, which the negative clause explicitly forbids.
   Because every prompt forbids text outright, none of these images can be individually wrong about a number - which is the failure mode this particular report exists to warn against.

rejected.idea: A wide hero banner behind the h1/subtitle (abstract flow field, particle stream, or soft gradient mesh).
rejected.why_not: Purely ornamental - it conveys no claim the title does not already make. It would push the three clickable report cards, which are the page's only actions and its heaviest objects in the top third, below the fold. On a readout-toned page it would read as a landing page trying to sell something.

rejected.idea: A bar chart of the five local models' CVTG-2K scores (0.9128 / 0.9116 / 0.8926 / 0.873 / ...).
rejected.why_not: The single worst idea on the list. The table already lists exact scores, and the top four differ by less than 0.04 - a chart would add no discriminating information while implying precision the numbers do not have. Worse, it would be a generated IMAGE OF A CHART, meaning every bar height and any axis value would be fabricated. In a report whose thesis is that generated numbers are ~75% trustworthy, a synthetic chart is an outright self-refutation. If a chart is wanted it must be drawn in markup, not generated.

rejected.idea: A neural-network / graph-of-nodes visual standing in for 'image models'.
rejected.why_not: The most generic AI-report image in existence; carries zero information specific to this page. It is also all-over high-frequency detail and luminous nodes - precisely the texture that would fight two dense tables for the reader's attention and drift toward the saturated blue the page reserves for --acc link meaning.

rejected.idea: A glossy photo-realistic GPU / server rack / PCIe card hero shot.
rejected.why_not: Wrong subject and wrong register. The report's claims are about model file sizes, VRAM headroom, and component count - not about hardware procurement, and no hardware recommendation is made anywhere. A polished product render also brings an advertising sheen that clashes with the forensic, measured tone, and its bright specular highlights would be the brightest thing on a near-black page.

rejected.idea: Per-row status icons on the table rows, or small icons on the three report cards.
rejected.why_not: Double-encoding. The .t-ok / .t-warn / .t-bad chips and the .win / .lose coloured cells already carry status, and the chips are only 10.5px type on a 4px radius - icons there would be unreadably small and would thicken the visual noise in the two densest blocks on the page. Icons also cannot honestly distinguish the report's most important distinction, which is provenance (author-reported vs measured vs third-party vs unverified), not merely pass/fail.

rejected.idea: An illustration of the CJK auto-verification trap - a magnifier or an eye inspecting a blurred field of glyphs.
rejected.why_not: This warning is real and worth an image on editorial grounds, but it cannot be drawn well under the no-text constraint. The subject IS glyphs; any honest depiction would either violate the constraint or abstract into an eye-over-blur cliche. It also leans on a stock-photography register (optics, inspection, scrutiny) that the page does not otherwise use. The card's prose and its bold 'it will lie' already land.

rejected.idea: A cost-tier comparison for the paid lane ($0.01 / $0.04 / $0.08-$0.11).
rejected.why_not: The cost column already gives exact figures and the prose already draws the comparisons ('~4x cheaper', '50% batch discount'). An image would restate the table at lower fidelity. There is also no spatial or proportional insight to gain here - the ratios are trivial arithmetic that the reader can do, unlike a 22.4-against-22.5 fit.

rejected.idea: A pipeline / roadmap illustration for the 'Recommended next step' section.
rejected.why_not: There is no roadmap. The section is two sentences and three URLs. A pipeline diagram implies stages and sequencing the plan does not have, which is exactly the kind of confident-looking fiction this report refuses to produce elsewhere.

images.caption: Two machined parts in the same tray: on the left a stack of components with a taller polished block overhanging the rim, on the right a single compact unit sitting with clear floor around it.
images.purpose: Makes the section-e argument spatial in one glance: three components plus an FP8-to-bf16 upcast overflow a fixed container that a single compact unit clears easily, which is what 'zero headroom on a 22.5 GB card' and 'one file, not three' actually mean. Prose states the numbers; this shows the geometry. This is also the caveat to the #1 pick - the container is finite and the alternative has room - so it earns its place twice.
images.prompt: A single wide, shallow bead-blasted aluminium tray, machined and anodised dark charcoal, photographed from a low three-quarter angle so the near rim runs across the bottom of the frame and the far wall recedes. Output for a 1.75:1 landscape frame, 1344 x 768 pixels, composed as a wide horizontal still life with generous empty ground. The tray is divided by one single hairline machined seam running front to back. On the left half, four separate machined blocks of differing footprints are stacked to near the rim, the tallest a polished mirror-finish block that sits proud of the tray edge and overhangs into darkness, casting a hard rectangular shadow onto the floor. On the right half, a single low compact anodised capsule, matte dark, sitting alone with a wide clear margin of empty tray floor visible on all four sides. Materials: bead-blasted and anodised aluminium, matte black polymer, one mirror-polished metal face. Lighting: one hard directional key from the upper left, cool blue-white with a faint 58a6ff sheen in the specular highlights, falling off steeply into near-black 0a0e14 corners; a single restrained warm d29922 glint along the overhanging block's exposed edge to mark it as the problem element; fill almost nil. Depth of field: shallow - the near rim and the overhang are sharp, the far wall softens gently. Palette strictly limited to near-black background 0a0e14, panel-shadow 111823, hairline grey-blue 1e2a38, pale highlight e6edf3, and sparse blue 58a6ff and amber d29922 accents. Mood: forensic, measured, cold, an evidence photograph of a physical constraint. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no labels, no arrows, no annotation of any kind anywhere in the frame.

images.caption: A dense grid of identical dark tiles in which roughly one tile in four is subtly chipped, cracked, or duller than the rest.
images.purpose: Makes the report's thesis - the baseline is about three characters in four correct - something the reader discovers with their own eye instead of taking on trust from bold text. The comprehension work is that the failures are ORDINARY and quiet: no catastrophically broken output, just a routine minority of small defects. That is the argument for why the official recipe does not fix it, and why transcription must be character-exact rather than eyeballed. The tile carries no markings precisely because the point is the defect RATE, not the glyphs.
images.prompt: A tight square field of small identical rounded-corner tiles set into a dark recessed panel in neat even rows and columns, filling the entire frame edge to edge. Output for a 1:1 square frame, 1024 x 1024 pixels, flat-on overhead framing with a slight angle so the rows recede. Most tiles are clean, evenly lit and perfectly identical; roughly one tile in four is subtly defective - a chipped corner, a hairline crack running to the edge, a slightly recessed face, a slightly proud face, or a duller matte finish. Every tile is a completely blank unmarked surface with nothing on it. Materials: matte ceramic or composite tiles, dark 111823 recesses between them, thin 1e2a38 grout lines, a few defective tiles with a very faint warm d29922 or f85149 tint deep in their recess so they read as flagged rather than colour-coded. Lighting: a low raking key from the upper left at a shallow angle so each small defect throws a tiny hard shadow and the clean tiles stay flat and even; a faint cool 58a6ff edge light along the top-left tile edges; falloff to near-black 0a0e14 at the far corners. Depth of field: shallow - the middle band of rows is sharp, the nearest and furthest rows soften. Palette strictly limited to background 0a0e14, panel 111823, hairline 1e2a38, pale highlight e6edf3, and sparse blue 58a6ff, amber d29922 and red f85149 accents. Mood: forensic, quiet, unsentimental, an inspection tray. Absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no digits, no characters, no glyphs, no writing, no symbols, no logos or marks of any kind anywhere on any tile.

images.caption: Three square specimen plates on a dark shelf at visibly different grades of finish, from rough and unlit through frosted to polished, with one matching bracket beside them left empty.
images.purpose: Gives the report's epistemic spine - which its numbers do not all carry the same weight - a visible form. Right now 'author-reported', 'No independent OCR benchmark exists yet', and the footer's primary / third-party / unverified promise are one italic phrase, two hedges, and a 12.5px dim line nobody reads. Graded surface finish is a material, wordless proxy for graded confidence, and the one empty slot stands for the independent verification that does not exist for the #1 pick. This image serves the reader's trust calibration more than any other element on the page could.
images.prompt: A vertical stack of three square specimen plates resting in shallow machined slots on a dark shelf, shot from slightly above and to the left at a three-quarter angle. Output for a 1:1 square frame, 1024 x 1024 pixels, composed as a compact vertical still life. The nearest plate is raw and unpolished - matte, pitted, a chipped edge, catching almost no light. The middle plate is frosted and etched, semi-translucent, softly lit. The farthest plate is polished and faintly self-luminous, catching a bright specular edge. Beside the stack, exactly one empty bracket or slot of the same square size, unlit and vacant. Materials: rough cast metal, frosted acrylic, glazed ceramic, machined dark shelf. Lighting: a single cool 58a6ff key from the upper left with one hard specular edge on the polished plate; a restrained warm d29922 rim along the rough nearest plate to mark it as unverified; deep falloff to a 0a0e14 background with 111823 midtones and 1e2a38 shadow separation; fill almost nil. Depth of field: pronounced - the nearest rough plate is sharply focused, the middle plate slightly soft, the farthest polished plate softly out of focus, which is what creates the ladder of confidence. Palette strictly limited to background 0a0e14, panel 111823, hairline 1e2a38, pale highlight e6edf3, and sparse blue 58a6ff and amber d29922 accents. Mood: archival, evidence locker, quiet and unsentimental. Absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no digits, no engraved inscriptions, no logos, no labels, no tags, no stamps, no writing of any kind on any plate.
